Hi Megan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and three asks to help our infra team size the pilot: 

Call recap:
- Primary use case: real-time payment confirmations and fraud hints in checkout flows (API calls originate from checkout browser + mid-tier).
- Expected peak traffic: ~4k concurrent active users, estimated 60 requests/s sustained, 150 requests/s burst.
- Payloads: short prompts (avg 220 tokens), often deterministic style with a handful of system instructions and user metadata.
- Priority: minimize time-to-first-token (TTFT) for perceived snappiness; streaming preferred for progressive UX.

Asks (to validate SLOs & streaming shape):
1) Target TTFT SLOs (please confirm): median ~120ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 600ms. If you have stricter internal targets, share them.
2) Streaming mode preference: you said SSE is preferred for browser clients — confirm whether WebSocket fallback is acceptable for mobile SDKs.
3) Heartbeat/sample-rate & chunk cadence: what UX cadence feels smooth for you? For example, do you need regular heartbeats every 200ms, or are 400ms intermittent chunks OK? Also, do you want per-chunk content (partial JSON objs) or plain text streaming?
4) Concurrency model & bursts: share whether you can buffer/retry from client side for transient delays, and an example burst profile (CSV is fine).

If you can reply with the small traffic sample and a single-day burst CSV (timestamps + rps), and confirm (1)-(3), I’ll loop in Karthik and Ben to propose a pilot config.

Thanks — Jordan

Hi Jordan — thanks, great summary. Answers inline below and attached a 24h sample burst CSV + a few example payloads.

1) TTFT SLOs: we want median <= 150ms, p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 700ms. The 150ms median is a hard UX bar for checkout.
2) Streaming: SSE is preferred for web. Mobile SDKs should use WebSocket (long-lived socket) if possible; fallback to polling is acceptable for older clients.
3) Heartbeat/cadence: for UX we expect an initial heartbeat within 100–200ms, then partial updates every ~250–350ms. Payloads should stream as text with chunked JSON lines (each chunk is a small JSON delta).
4) Concurrency/bursts: attached CSV has the 5-min peak we saw last month (peaks at 180 rps). We can cap client concurrency to 6 requests per user across tabs. Retries: clients retry after exponential backoff; must tolerate transient 5xxs.

Pilot timeline: we're targeting a pilot start next week (week of Apr 12). Can Redwood run an A/B with 5% traffic for two days?

Thanks — Megan

Jordan / Ben — quick technical feasibility notes and recommended pilot config: 

Feasibility: overall achievable on Hosted with a tuned path, Dedicated recommended if they want consistent p95/p99 under sustained bursts. p99 700ms is tight but doable with warmstart and KV cache priming (warm cache hit-rate target >90%).

Suggested pilot config (5% traffic A/B):
- Model variant: open-compat quantized variant (8-bit) we tested for similar prompt lengths.
- Serving lane: dedicated soft-reserve pool (2 x A100-equivalent) for pilot windows to absorb bursts.
- Batching: dynamic micro-batching capped at 6 concurrency slots per worker, 50ms batch wait upper bound for small aggregation without harming TTFT.
- KV cache: size to hold ~10k session keys; keep 2GB cache per GPU for their payload distribution.
- Warmstart: pre-warm 30s before rollout and keep a minimum warm concurrency of 20 slots.
- Heartbeat & chunk cadence: SSE heartbeats at initial <200ms can be produced by emitting an empty chunk ("hb") on first token then regular delta chunks every ~300ms. Recommend chunking content into ~200–400 token deltas or 150–300ms cadence to match UX.
- Backpressure & fallback: if queue depth grows > 75%, route to a cheaper model variant with graceful degradation message. WebSocket fallback fine for mobile.

Operational notes:
- Telemetry: capture per-token latency, first-byte, and chunk-emit timestamps. Configure a p95/p99 alert on first-token latency and a rolling error budget for 5xx spikes.
- Probe script: run 2-hour synthetic with their burst CSV at 1:1 and monitor p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and for chunk cadence consistency.
- Risks: cold-start spikes, KV cache eviction under heavy multi-tenant load, client-side retry storms increasing RPS.

Next steps I can own: create a pilot runbook (ops playbook + probe script) and proposed rollout JSON. Ben — can you size the Dedicated lanes and estimate cost delta for 2 A100-equivalents for 48 hours?

Will produce runbook by EOD Sun.
